title: Forfeiture of Closing Cost Credits on Withdrawn, Denied or Lapsed Loan Files
content:
When a loan file will not close, the Larkspur Closing Cost Credits on it are forfeited.

**Rule.** When the loan file is withdrawn, denied, closed for incompleteness or lapses for want of intent to proceed, every reserved or verified credit on it is forfeited, and any booked balance is forfeited with the reason that the loan did not close. A revoked credit forfeits its balance with the reason that a program change made it ineligible, and an expired credit with the reason that it expired. A forfeiture entry names the award or payout entry it draws on and carries the whole remaining balance; nothing is ever paid to the borrower in cash. A credit on a withdrawn file does not move to a new application; the new file reserves afresh.

### Reasons recorded on the forfeiture entry

| What happened | Credits affected | Reason on the forfeiture entry |
|---|---|---|
| Loan file withdrawn, denied, closed for incompleteness or lapsed for want of intent to proceed | every reserved or verified credit on the file | the loan did not close |
| Credit revoked | that credit | a program change made it ineligible |
| Credit expired | that credit | the credit expired |

### Questions the rule answers

**Is any part of a forfeited balance paid to the borrower?** No. The forfeiture entry carries the whole remaining balance, and nothing is paid in cash.

**If the borrower withdraws and starts a new application, does the credit follow?** No. The credit on the withdrawn file does not move; the new file reserves afresh.

**What does a forfeiture entry point to?** The award or payout entry it draws on.

### Illustration (hypothetical)

A verified Larkspur First Home Credit has a booked balance of 2500.00 when its loan file is denied. The credit is forfeited, and one forfeiture entry of 2500.00, drawing on the credit's award entry, is booked with the reason that the loan did not close.
